thread:
Cam: did a pass on the routing policies editor today. a few UX things that popped up during usability testing
Cam: 1) people expect a numeric priority to be editable in-line (e.g., click the 1/2/3 and type). we currently only support drag reorder which confuses them
Riya: inline edit makes sense. how would it affect drag interactions? maybe show a small edit icon on hover and switch to text input on click
Owen: caveat: if we let them type arbitrary numbers we need to normalize (e.g., gaps, duplicates). backend currently uses array index for ordering so we'll need a reconciliation step 
Priya (PM): goal: keep drag for quick reordering, allow direct edit for precise placement. UX approach: editing a number should move the rule to closest slot and animate. Add a tooltip: 'Typing changes order'
Sam (a11y): accessibility: the numeric control needs clear labelling and ARIA live region announcing the new order when changed. keyboard users expect +/- stepper or arrow key adjustments too
Cam: another thing: validation badges on rules are subtle (tiny orange dot). users miss them. suggestion: use a pill with icon + short text (e.g., 'Conflict: priority') and tooltip on hover with remediation steps
Riya: agreed. also the color contrast of the pill needs to meet AA. Sam, can you propose colors?
Sam (a11y): suggest dark amber (#b56500) for bg with white text, and 4.5:1 contrast. also include an icon with aria-hidden and text for screenreader. ensure focusable so keyboard users can open remediation help
Owen: on preview sandbox: when users simulate a request, they expect to see which rule matched and why. current preview only shows final route. Can we add 'matched conditions' and a small diff of attribute checks?
Priya (PM): yes. two-pane preview: left = sample payload + controls, right = step-by-step match result with the matched rule highlighted. add small 'why not' toggles for non-matching rules
Cam: microcopy nits: change 'Match example' label to 'Sample request' and replace 'Preview' CTA with 'Simulate' in the editor to clarify intent
Riya: noted. also UX flow: when user clicks 'Simulate' and then edits rules, keep the simulation open and auto-recompute with a small toast 'Simulation updated' rather than closing it
Owen: perf note: recomputing on every minor edit could be heavy. debounce 400ms and show 'Recomputing...' overlay. if heavy backend call, show skeleton states
Sam (a11y): keyboard flow: after simulation runs, focus should land on the matched rule panel so screenreader users can hear the result; don't trap focus but provide skip link back to editor
design-bot: upload: https://redwood.screenshots/ci/1820345678/inline-number-edit.png :camera_flash:
Priya (PM): next steps: Riya to mock inline numeric edit + pill validation states; Sam to provide color tokens and aria patterns; Owen to scope backend ordering normalization; Cam will update content strings for labels
Cam: adding a small helper in the empty-state of the rules list: 'Tip: try numbering rules for precise order or drag to rearrange' 
Riya: I'll iterate mocks and post Figma link in this thread by EOD
Owen: I'll prototype order-normalize logic in a branch and link PR here
Sam (a11y): I'll draft keyboard interaction doc and include aria-live examples to paste into the component's README
Priya (PM): thanks team. will pull this into the sprint and assign tasks.
